ques: hi bill, your keyboard playing is very inspiring; do you have any tips on how to practice hand independence? it feels quite overwhelming as a process, i'm not exactly sure on how to babystep my way into that. thabks
answ: this is actually a relationship for more than 2. your right hand, your left hand, your voice, another person as the bass player, another singer, another person as a guitar/keyboard player, ...... Check around your ensemble (maybe just you) and tally up HOW MANY of those items are in your ensemble. (i listed 6 things, now that i count them). And now, keep in mind that there are maybe only THREE ROLES that those must play, IN TOTAL. not each. Basically it's 3 jobs to do. so think about how many people/things are doing them. If the amount of things/people doing the jobs is more or less than 3, then there will have to be some interesting agreements made. everyone probably can't/shouldn't do all 3 at the same time, unless they are very very coordinated with each other. And yet, on the other hand, if there's only 2 things/people, they will have to juggle the 3 roles. the 3 roles are bass, melody, chords. So let me give you some examples, and my point is that your hands have different jobs depending on the personell situation. so for example: let's say it's just you. and let's say you are using both hands and your voice. that's pretty clear, your left hand takes the bass, your right hand takes the chords mostly, and your voice takes the melody. Well, imagine, instead, that you already have a bass player in the band, and let's say you are NOT singing. In that case, the bass player plays the bass, and YOU will be playing NOT the bass, but the melody and chords -- probably 1 with each hand. This is an entirely different configuration because now you are playing chords with your left hand. Let's imagine a different situation-- let's say you are playing with no bass player, you are not singing, but you have another person who is the singer. In this case, you will be doing bass in left hand and chords on right. Let's look at another example: if it's you on keyboard, and someone else on guitar, and the guitar player is singing. Well, the 2 of you need to come to an agreement and one of you should take care of the bass, and the other should take care of the chords. An important hint is that there should not be more than 1 person taking care of the bass (unless it is written EXACTLY, AND if it's neccesary to be full of BEEF at that particular moment.-- this will only be good for a non-musical sound effect / rumble sound. will not really work musically/tonally.) Also the other combination i forgot to mention is, if you are playing piano by yourself with no other players and not using your voice-- in that case, you will be dividing the 3 roles amongst only TWO players (your 2 hands) so in that case, you sort of have to magically somehow juggle the 3 of them. So, between different combinations of bass, chords, melody, ... and the players: your left hand, your right hand, and your voice, there are many different combinations for what jobs your hands are going to play. So it's important to take a moment to notice which of these scenarios you are in. And beyond that, the strategy is essentially the same, which is to use your imagination and try to play songs in any possible way you can, because someone's gotta do it

So the fear was that some terribly unexpected stuff may happen around the world as a result of all the computer systems suddenly thinking it's 1900, instead of 2000. there was a widespread fear that everything would break down. but luckily, through hard work i think, most of the important systems managed to get fixed in time, so there really wasn't any huge catastrophe. answ: just start playing 2 strokes each hand, evenly, at some reasonable pace like 2 per beat, at 120bpm, and just speed up the tempo gradually. your hands will eventually figure out what you need to do. like that time when you learned to walk. actually wait i just remembered, here's a slightly more interesting tip .... try playing it so that the second note is actually the downbeat instead of the first note. so do like a RLLR-RLLR etc pattern, so the second stroke is the one that falls on the downbeat. and then gradually speed up from there. this way is actually very healthy to learn because it probably helps even out the strokes, by psychologically reversing the way your mind thinks of them. i just remembered that probably 80% of the doublestrokes i play are aligned this way, it's just more comfortable for me. it frees the pairs from prison of their pairing, if that makes sense. allows for stronger integration with singles actually, with more possibilities for sure. in other words it will help them not sound like doubles

ques: why is it so much easier to start a new song than to continue one?? it's driving me crazy. you'd think continuing something would be easier than coming up with something from scratch, but no. i'm guessing you're going to answer with "try making shorter songs", but that doesn't solve the problem because it doesn't train the skill of coming up with "the next part" of a song. i think learning to play already existing songs on an instrument could help train that intuition, what do you think about that?
answ: here's what happened to me. when i was at your stage, one solution is to just finish it in 1 session. i was writing entirely on paper at that time. but i soon got tired of that method (it's a good method, but it results in some pretty mentally insane songs, with all due respect to mental insanity), and i also came up with a lot of choruses, verse fragments, or just intros, and didn't know how or WHEN to deal with them. but here's what i eventually did: i went through all my notes and collected every song or song fragment i had ever written or worked on. and i put them all into a list in chronological order. Then, i just started at the beginning of the list, and 'find the next thing' or, just 'answer the next question' on each of them, before moving onto the next one. this unfortunately would take infinite years, so i shuffled things up a little and did a percentage completion system, etc etc, but still had ways of selecting which one i was doing next. nowadays i'm selecting to record, which means whichever one i select, could be a fragment, is the one i will record. so that puts me in a situation of writing for the recording which is about to happen. I guess what i'm trying to say is, the selection process is so important because if you are not confident about the validity of your selection, then you will run away from the song. So i guess the selection is one half of the challenge. then there's just techniques to do once you're there and you're already sure you're working on the right song, now what do you do? Well it's a lot like being a doctor. you just have to ask good questions. First thing i would check, is, 'is this the beginning', like, does the piece you have belong at the beginning of the song, or in the middle, is it the chorus, etc etc. If it clearly belongs absolutely at the total beginning, then, the process is pretty simple. Just run it through, and stop playing at the end of what you have, and wait for lightning to strike. Then if it doesn't, ask as many questions as you can about what you think you might have been about to hear.... Then what i do, for a re-set, is i walk over and touch the door handle, and come back and run it again from the top, and do the same thing again. It's extremely important that you run it AT TEMPO (at the right tempo) because often what we do in songwriting if we're trying to think of ideas, we run the bit before, over and over and we start doing it faster, which will trick you into then writing things at the wrong tempo and it won't fit with the rest. so make sure all your run throughs are at tempo. it's good to get on the metronome as soon as you can, to preserve, because songwriting is a time warp and it can make things change speed when you didn't mean to. But i didn't mention what to do if the piece you have is NOT the beginning. in this case you are going to have to do a weird backwards puzzle to figure out what comes before. It's almost impossible to figure out what comes before something, actually. one weird trick which might be semi-reliable is to run the chorus and see if you can get a second verse, and then hope that one of the things around there also makes sense as an intro, but at least for me writing backwards is almost impossible

ques: I find "just did a bad thing" to be very well orchestrated/composed. How did you figure out which instruments to use in the song and what parts they should play? Do you follow a formula per se or do you do it randomly?
answ: here's what i've discovered: i choose all the instruments i want first. then i go through the song and figure out where each one goes. instead of going to a place, and finding the instrument, i first get the instrument, and then find where it fits. i call this the sprinkle technique. This actually won't take care of the entire song, because if you only do sprinkles, you will usually never end up getting the important mainstays like the kick and bass, etc, but, it is a good technique nonetheless. it is particularly exciting when you do sprinkles first, before doing anything else. by the way this only works if you've written the song first before you start recording it, and have the exact road map

basically you could just start with one note. just play that note, now you know how it feels to play that note. so you have 2 options: playing the note, or playing nothing. think of the wonderous portraits you could paint, just from painting and not painting that note. objectivity and subjectivity are tools to determine which person is right and which person is wrong. the person who knows the words 'objectivity' and 'subjectivity' is always right, and here's how they do it: first they say 'subjectively', which means people are allowed to disagree. Then, they provide an alternate situation, 'objectively', which means there is only one right answer and you are not allowed to disagree with that. It's sort of like a good cop / bad cop scenario, where the 'subjectivity' scenario gives you a false sense of comfort, thinking it's ok for people to have different opinions, then the hammer comes down when 'objectively' there is only one true opinion, which spells checkmate for the other person of course

ques: how does daylight saving time actually work?
answ: during the spring and summer months, the clock tells you a later time than it actually is. so it makes the evening seem a little lighter and the morning a little darker. this is besides the fact that the evening and morning are both already lighter than they were in the winter, but because of daylight saving, the evening is WAY more lighter, and the morning is ..... only a little bit lighter. it shifts the daylight later by 1 hour. in the springtime, when it changes, you will always hear people saying 'wow i can't believe it's still light at this time of evening', and in the fall when it switches back, you will hear people saying, 'wow i can't believe it's already dark at this time of evening.' However, what you may not hear, but is still said, is similar but reversed comments about the morning. But with a different twist, because it goes in the opposite direction of the way it's been heading. so, for example, in the springtime in the morning, after it changes, people in the early morning will be saying 'well, the mornings have been gradually getting lighter these past few weeks, but they just suddenly got darker again, although i know they are still going to gradually get ligher from here.' and in the fall, in the morning, just after it changes back, people in the early morning will say 'well, the mornings have been getting gradually darker over the past few weeks, but suddenly they just got brighter again, although i know they still will continue to get darker from here.'

ques: When do you plan to release ur next video.

ques: how did the sign in im best friends with my own front door get bad bad
answ: i'll tell you exactly how it happened. i was on a brand new break-neck schedule, where i was supposed to finish a song/video every 2 weeks, which was so much tighter than i had ever previously done it (at least 4x quicker), that no one believed was possible. so this is supposedly the first song of this new scheme, which essentially seems more like a dare at this point, because it's so absurd. So i had spent an entire day songwriting and i pretty much only made it through 2 stanzas. so the next day i had to kick myself and realize that this schedule is so ridiculous that i need to finish the song in the next 4 hours or it's pretty much game over. the 'sign' bit is the first bit to be written under that assumption. so in a way you can probably assume that this is the feeling of realizing i am going to have to steamroll the entire remainder of the songwriting process for this song. And i should clarify, steamrolling sometimes leads to fantastic growth, and i am thrilled with where the song ends up going, especially toward the end. and i don't think it would have ever gone like that, had the prior steamrolling not occured. it's a lesson that continues to play out again and again in the creative process, in the context of a world with limited time and resources

ques: what's a song writing process look like for you? do you have something set you do every time or is it just organic?
answ: at any time, anywhere, ideas can fall on me. even in dreams. that is one part of the process. learning to catch these is crucial to this part of the process. about 70% of the strongest ideas come unexpectedly, not during a songwriting session. So they must be captured and cataloged properly. At that time usually no work is done beyond the capture of the idea. Alternatively, to generate ideas, a more deliberate idea generation session can occur. this is planned, when you try to come up with ideas. remembering a key principle which is that songs can come from literally anywhere, there may be various clever strategies about which places to look. the fun part is, because they can come from anywhere, there is no limit to the places you can look. But still, this is just idea generation, separate from the remainder of the songwriting work. it's still just an idea generation session. Then there is the 'work', which is when you tend to entries in the catalog. depending on the situation, you may be tasked to finish an entire item, or just part of it, before moving onto another. But in either case, you are essentially playing hospital with the song. diagnose it, figure out what it is, what it wants to be, what it's meant to be, etc, and make decisions accordingly. 95% of the time i work strictly forwards, only being concerned with what comes next, and continuing along in order, forwards. The only situation where i would be forced to work backwards is if the original idea does not belong at the beginning. then it's a puzzle to fill in what came before, which seems to defy all laws of physics for me. very unusual. but it can be done and there are various tricks which work with varying degrees of effectiveness. So the majority of the songwriting process (basically all of it except the initial idea seed) follows the same idea of figuring out what comes next. so there are a few important practices that always seem to hold true. agree on an exact tempo as soon as you can, and run a metronome to keep from drifting. this avoids a crisis where you've drifted the tempo and now you may be writing at a level of density which is never gonna fit at the same tempo as what you've already written elsewhere in the song. another important concept is the fact that you really only know what's best the FIRST time you hear it. so you have to do whatever you can to protect this authentic, real time run through, from the mindset of never having heard it before. of course, when you're working, you're inevitably gonna hear it many times. a standard trick i use to help 're-set' is to walk to the door and touch the door handle (with the metronome running) and return and run-through from the beginning. it's also important to remember, full run-throughs are much much more valuable than only running the last part. the full-run through is the only thing that's going to truly reveal where we are at, at a certain point in the song, and thus to properly determine what happens (or does not happen) next. Another thing to realize, if nothing seems to be working and you keep trying things and ditching them, it's important to recognize that the ideas get worse the more you reject them. so if you reject 3 ideas, the 4th will be worse. so if you get too deep into a hole of rejecting, it can be useful to recognize that the first one might be the best one you're gonna get, and make extra effort to try to make the first one work, because in that case it's usually your best shot. Finally, another interesting trick which i've been using a lot recently is, pretend it's in a video. pretend it's taking place in a movie, inside a story. This doesn't even mean you're gonna write a video, but sometimes just pretending it's taking place in a video, will immediately cause interesting songwriting to materialize effortlessly. it's bizarre, because many times when this technique is working, it's not even associated with any particular video content. it's just because you told yourself to pretend you are thinking of visual content, this somehow creates an automatic trigger for songwriting

ques: In "La de da de da de da de day oh" you rhymed "mall" 3 times, was there any hidden meaning behind that?
answ: yes, this is what it is: After selecting this song for recording, i felt deep dread and regret the next day. basically there is a lot of anxiety around selecting a song to record and do a music video for, because unfortunately, for some unknown reason, i always make my songrecordings and videos very complicated. so it is a large commitment when choosing a song. At the time of selection, the song was only written up to the end of the first chorus. So i was feeling a deep amount of regret, the day after selecting it. but changing it would increase all doubts all around, because it had been a very thorough selection process, and if i invalidated that it would cast even larger shadows of doubt on the entire ability to select a song. So i was sitting in the waiting chairs for a haircut, just being very unsure of how to carry forward with the song, ... i had already attempted to change my mind earlier in the morning, to a much slower and sadder song. and i found myself circling back again to 'la de da', and just at the exact moment i was getting into the haircut chair, i let my mind turn to what i think might happen next, in the writing. obviously we are going into the second verse. And it's moments like these, when we say 'what if', that suddenly a blitz of writing comes. The first 3 lines of the second verse came at me very quickly. the relentlessness of the word 'mall' had a nice momentum to it, and certainly helped to plunge me into confidence that the song was the right choice, and by the time i got into the chair, i was certain i would be doing that song. the 4th line, however, did not come at all, and i had to force it later in the actual writing session and i am to this day not proud of it. so if i could summerize the answer to your original question, the meaning of the triple mall is 'momentum'

ques: do you ever find it difficult to put your song ideas into the song?
And if yes how do you manage to do so?
answ: occasionally

first, i must figure out whether the 'idea' is supposed to be the beginning of the song, or not the beginning. if it's the beginning, then just run through it in real time and then have more ideas while already in the song. if the idea is the middle, this is much more difficult because then you have to figure out what came before, which is like writing backwards. which for me is almost impossible. but i have developed some tricks for this, such as asking a trillion questions, trying 100 things, or, seeing what comes AFTER, and then continue from there and hope that somewhere along the line a beginning reveals itself in some kind of cyclical construct

ques: if you wouldn't mind temporarily stepping out of the mindset of producing your newest and soon-too-be-hopefully-greatest song and video, is there any song you've made in the past that stands out to you in any way;

answ: yes

on 'hallelujah', i decided to START the entire recording process on an EQ setting that mimics the speaker on a smartphone. the reason i did this was to try to have a better guarantee that the arrangement would make sense there (literally no bass). it sometimes stresses me out that that platform is so drastically different from the ones that include the bass (headphones, car speakers, etc). It's almost like if you are doing a TV show and 40% of your audience can't see the color green. If you are making the project on a system where you CAN see the color green, you're gonna have no idea what those greenless viewers are even seeing. Some people check different systems at the very end, and then make 'adjustments', but i figured it's way too late if you check it at the end. so i decided to start the entire process in the bassless mode, to make sure i was making decisions that were strong on that platform. Then turn the bass frequencies back on and then fill in the bass i want for the full-range listeners. This seemed like a good idea but it didn't really go so well and i don't do it anymore. it didn't really harm the sound of the song, but it encouraged me to overthink even more than i normally do

ques: ik this is a tired type of question, but whats the inspiration/meaning behind your video Time Mop? it's very different than other things you were making at the time and gives off some weird vibes.
answ: there are 2 elements to that, which came about completely separately. the audio, and the video that goes with it. The audio recording, called "time mop", was part of a series of 4 recordings i made in june 2009. my career felt way way too speculative for many years up until then, and i was getting very desperate to actually make some recordings. so in a fit of rage and desperation, i did "help, i'm trapped in the center of a rectangle", and 3 others, including "time mop". those are just instrumental music pieces, with no video. Then, later, around 2014, after i had finally begun actually making videos, sometimes song-videos, one of the types of videos i was doing would be music videos to go with songs i had already recorded. i had done some of these already, and they all were songs with lyrics. When there's lyrics, it usually gives you a pretty obvious guide for what might happen in the video. But, what if it's an entirely instrumental song? what would the video look like then? So i decided to try. Actually, i just remembered, i had actually begun to do work on this video as early as 2013, in the early stages of experimenting with video. and then i picked it up again after the regular video production schedule was underway. So it was originally an instrumental, in 2009, as a challenge to myself to do ANYTHING (besides textual non-video non-music), and the video in 2013 was a challenge to see if i could do a music video for a song without lyrics

ques: why was the time between the draft composition/writing of "and the day goes on" and its release date 699 days?
answ: i will explain the timeline so hopefully it will make sense. in march 2015, the instrumental idea for the verse occured to me. i was not expecting it, it was not a planned 'writing session'. This is how many songs get started, they drop out of the sky, so you have to get good at catching them. So, this is me catching it. (march 2015). Sure, i could have immediately gone into a writing session for that idea, but, why not instead for an idea i had had the previous day? or a video idea i had had the previous day? it is always raining ideas. There is always more to be done than there is time to do. In march 2015 i had developed a 2 pronged approach: 2 short videos per week, and 'everything else'. I was doing 2 short videos per week just to have something to release, then in between, move forward on longer projects. I had a randomized selection scheme to help choose which longer projects to do. Near to that time, the 'crazy/raining' song was selected. That took several weeks. After that, it was the 'free to do whatever you want to' song. This took even longer. What also was happening at the same time was, my short videos had taken off on the vine platform. So i had made the decision to start vinifying my entire video catalog starting with the earliest, and posting them to vine every day. Around august (2015) i reached the end of the catalog so i had to make a decision about what to do going forward. i decided the vines were doing so well that it became important to make 7 new ones per week. This was unfortunate for my longer video aspirations, because it pretty much meant zero time leftover to pursue that. but it was important to keep things rolling on vine. So i carried on like this for about 2 more months, but my desire to make long videos was getting even more intense. I discovered a trick, where i could spend the first half of the day working on a long video, and not start the vine until the second half of the day, which forced me to do them much quicker. so i started on history of japan (oct 2015). i continued on like this, doing short videos while doing a long video, and finally around january i was getting into the scoring process (final stage) of the japan video and decided that i should pause the vines in order to finish the japan video more quickly. japan was finished by late january, it went to youtube and did very well there. i took this as a chance to put together a project i had always really really wanted to do but never found time: to make videos out of journal edits. i had about 6 years of audio journal content, and i combed through it as best i could, making video edits to attempt to chronicle my journey. After about 2 months working on this, i really had to cut it short because it was going on way too long. so i really only got to do about 10% of what i wanted. Also the other half of that project was for improv footage. I had to cut that way way short because no regular videos were being done during this time. So i only got a chance to do maybe 2% of the improv edits i wanted to do. So finally around May (2016) i was ready to get back to regular videos. there was so much i wanted to do, and didn't even know where to begin. I started extremely short, as i normally do, with a plan to make them gradually longer. I started making an agenda list of the sequence of upcoming items, and i wanted to include some medium length songs. Choosing from a list of hundreds, one of the ones i chose was that instrumental chord sequence back from march 2015. So i wrote that into a full song, over a couple of days. this song was called 'and the day goes on.' Among other short videos, there was also another song that i selected at that time, for release soon after. which i also wrote fully at that time. called 'hallelujah'. we are around june 2016 now. Then, suddenly, i felt a lot of public outrage that i was 'still doing short videos', and to be honest, i agreed with it. I also had a pent up desire to do an even more bombastic history project than the japan one, so i changed the plans, cancelled the remaining short-medium projects, and started on history of the entire world. Something you may or may not know about the history of the world- the world has a lot of history. so, to put it all into 1 video is probably impossible, so i knew i was taking on something that might be impossible. but i wanted to do it anyway. so first i had to *learn* the history of the entire world. which also takes a long time. research and writing took all summer, and i reached the end of the writing by about September 7, 2016. One of the things i had been thinking during the writing process, is a 2D equirectangular projected map is probably not gonna work for this. i should really get it on a 3D globe. but i didn't have the tools for that. so during most of september i was experimenting with various 3D tools to try to meet my 3D needs. i also began going through and developing the images that would be needed for the video, while also making many changes to the script. By the end of october i had most of this squared away, and around November 1st i was ready to begin the full video production. At this point i was determined to reach the end of the entire project by december 1st, and i nearly destroyed myself throughout november trying to meet this. but toward the end of november i realized this wasn't even close to possible. so i continued through december, through many of the most challenging parts of the video production, especially having to correct some problems with the 3D globe animations (which had been first done in october). finally made it to the end of the visual production by about february 7 (2017), and began on recording the final narration, and doing the final jingles, and then finally doing the score. the video was finally finished around may 10, 2017. By this time i knew very well that i really just need to do songs for the rest of my life. So i decided to skip the videos and just do audio songs, 1 per week. this went ok, but i soon realized that videos are very important. so around late june (2017) i started on 2 projects simultaneously: a freeform non-song video (hi, i'm steve) and a music video for one of the recently released audio songs (movie star). Working on 2 things at once is usually a recipe for failure, so i did then one at a time. steve first, then movie star. Then onward, to the next music video, 'outside'. this took about 6 weeks. I've never been pleased by the amount of time it takes to do these things. my prefered target for music videos would be 1 week, but to this day i've never been able to accompish this. Nearing the end of the 'outside' project, in late september (2017), i made a demand of myself that i MUST do these in 2 weeks. and i also felt it was necessary to do non-songs as well. So, alternate betwen non-songs and songs, and also, 1 out of every 2 songs should have live performance footage. So the next item would be a non-song, and, because i was able to make it shorter, i was able to do it just barely in 2 weeks. this was called 'soap tips' and was completed around oct 10, 2017. The next thing would have to be a song, and it would have to include live performance footage. Unfortunately this shattered all previous records for how long a music video should take, and this is probably because i hadn't appeared in live performance footage in such a long time that i couldn't stop myself from being incredibly particular for how things appear. i was horrified by the fact that that project ultimately took exactly the same amount of time as history of japan had taken (98 days, or 14 weeks.) it was finally completed in january, 2018. the target of course was 2 weeks, but that was a hopeless failure. So my next revision of the plan, would be to do 2 weeks per video, but they don't have to be a song. because i knew song videos would take longer, probably because my standards for how long a song should be were somewhere around 2:30 to 3:30, where as the non-song videos could be as short as 1 minute or maybe even less. so i decided to just try 1 video per 2 weeks, not necessarily a song. I was able to succeed at this, just barely, with 2 non-song videos. But, of course, as fate would have it, i realized songs are incredibly important. So i decided to do a song next, i already knew i wanted to do 'and the day goes on', because that one had its writing completed (in 2016) and i thought it was a strong one that i was confident about. I decided 4 weeks would be a sensible target for that. it was an especially elegant target, because it was february, and in that year (most years) februrary is exactly 4 weeks, so that would put the release date on exactly the same day of the month as the previous. Unfortunately that proved again to be impossible. and it never helps that my standards usually continue to go up. I was very meticulous on most parts of the process. i finally was able to complete the video around april 25, 2018. i immediately moved on to start the next song project. It's worth mentioning what happens next, because that will help bring this into even more perspective for you. At the start of every song process, i first do a generalized idea having process, where i come up with brand new ideas for songs. I usually do about 5 or 10, THEN the song selection process begins, where those new ideas are put into the much larger pool of unfinished songs, and i select from the entire list. It looks like there were 9 new ideas created on april 26 and 27, 2018. What ended up being selected, for the next song, was none of those, it was one that was already in the broader list ('hello sexy pants'). But, of those new 9, many of those have been extremely strong contenders every time since, with many of them almost getting picked, and one of them being 'when i get older' which was picked later that year. To get back to your original question, i think one of the strongest factors in play here is the fact that it is impossible to do everything at the same time, although that would be extremely convenient for me

ques: i keep having ideas when it's hard to write them down (shower etc.) and if i do go to write the idea down i usually forget most of the details. and if i deliberately put myself into a situation where i can easily write things down (usually by having my ideas document open or by using an audio recorder), then i can't have ideas. it feels like it's only possible for me to either have ideas or remember them, but not both.
answ: that's true, ideas come most easily when they would be harder to write down. There are 2 strategies for the shower. one strategy, if you think the idea is really that good, just get out of the shower and go write it down. Or, if you don't want to do that, here are some memory tricks. pretend you are explaining the idea to someone else, and start explaining it in as many technical ways as you can. Pretend you have to explain it to them so that they can reproduce the idea exactly, but, you are not allowed to actually demonstrate it. For example, if it's a sentence, say "the first word is ___, the second word is ____," etc... Count the words. remind yourself how many words there are. Say all the odd numbered words. Say all the even numbered words. Think of the first letter of each word, and put all those letters together. try to come up with an alternate sentence using the same starting letters. Try to access the idea in as many different ways as you can. If it is a musical idea, start thinking of the notation of it, imagine you are explaining the musical notation to someone else without singing it. List the notes in order. Count the notes. List the rhythmic values in order. If you don't know musical notation in this way, hopefully you have some other conceptual notation system you use to think about notes and time. What tempo is it? what song has a similar tempo? how many notes are in the first beat? how many notes are in the second beat? etc etc etc. Keep trying to access the idea on as many mental avenues as you can, and this will increase the likelyhood that you will be able to retrieve it. but really the best option is to just get out of the shower. Most other places besides the shower, try to carry a recording device with you, the most common one being a smart phone. and if you have that, then much of these techniques will not be necessary

ques: How did you predict 2020 in "just did a bad thing"? "All the things I'm supposed to do / and the places I'm supposed to go are cancelled"
What is the real meaning behind this line?
answ: things predict themselves. that's what i like about songwriting, it opens the door for things to do what they're gonna do

here's what i think, as i'm analyzing it now: this is a classic case of the song being about itself. The starting point for that song was just the one line ('just did a bad thing'), with really no indication of any sort of form or anything. Half way through the first section, it already seems to ditch out of the original paradigm slightly ('wondering what it is, etc'), it slips into the major key, and just,... no sort of repeating figure has been established. so far everything seems to be a special-case scenario. Then when it hits the next stanza, (bad day, bad year), we've already broken from what it had done in the first stanza. (the first stanza had the 'regret' line, which is quite different from the first line, but in the second stanza, the first two lines essentially are the same as each other), so for many reasons, at this point, (after 'bad year'), it's very clear that there is NO established pattern. we are free to roam. And it's likely at this point that i was feeling stuck, because really there's just too many possibilities. I was probably running through what i had so far, thinking i would get clues about the future (of the song) from the past (in the song). And that's just not gonna happen, because really what should probably happen is it should probably get out and GO somewhere it hasn't gone yet. So, looking at what did come next, the 'cancelled' line, this is a perfect way of expressing that everything you might have expected was going to happen (based on what happened so far) in the song, will probably not happen. And, sure enough, immediately after this, it transitions into a totally new key, and a new paradigm entirely. So basically the reason for that line is to shake off the previous paradigm (bad things, etc), because we gotta get away and jump into a whole new territory. (the 'game' section, etc). As far as anything having resemblence to future world events, well, this is always more likely to happen the more songs i write. when making a case that something predicted something, you can always ignore the ones that didn't fit. such as 'at the airport terminal' which certainly does not predict 2020

I've done it. But i also paralyze myself with the fear that what I write won't be world-altering, which of course it won't be - i haven't done a lot of writing so I don't have the practice.

a fun fact about world-altering: it's actually possible to do certain things that seem so NON world altering, that it actually seems world-altering in its level of non-world-altering. ques: you say that you try not to use nonsensical lyrics, yet on the surface some of your lyrics are easy to interpret as nonsensical, so i'm curious.
what was the meaning behind the first verse of "i'm best friends with my own front door"?
answ: i'm curious if you are just reading them, with no music. they're not guaranteed to work like that

basically i was starting on a new experiment: finish an entire music video in 2 weeks or die trying. i was sick of failure, i had been trying to do this and kept failing. the previous several videos all took 8 weeks or more. and i just was so desperate and felt like my life was passing me by, so i just snapped and demanded myself to succeed at 2 weeks. So i'm going through the (long) list of songs and song ideas to choose from, and, ...... it's just not working. i'm going through the list for hours, not finding one i want to do. So at some point, my brain just said "what would the song you Want to do now sound like?" and spontaneously the first line hit me, and i knew immediately that that would be the next song. So i already know it feels right, seems right, means very much to me, etc, but, when i think about it i can also explain why this is. It's like i'm developing a friendliness toward the idea of just... walking out the front door. Just being honest with my situation, ... etc. and picking this next song should be something as easy as just opening the front door, in a friendly manner. Now the second line, again this all came to me instinctually, but i'm just trying to think about it now and explain it.... the second line ('i just closed it but it's opening more') .... this gets deeper because there is the feeling that even if i've failed to notice how easy things could be, ... the door is actually opening on its own. We all know we have the tendency to sometimes overlook the friendly and obvious choices in life, so i think this line gives me a pretty strong feeling because it's like it's saying, even if you miss it, the opportunity will grow more to make you notice it. And the next 2 lines, ('then the cops came and they sent me to jail, but tomorrow i'm gonna open it again'), and again this is not supposed to necessarily work good without the music. so please take this only in the context of the way it sounds in the song. So these 2 lines seem to be basically doubling down on this optimism: the 3rd line is like "nope, youre gonna get punished for taking the easy route", then the 4th line shows determination to overcome this. Another bit of optimism is tucked in here also because most jails don't let you open the door. So you're just saying, tomorrow you're gonna get another chance to easily and friendily open a door that was previously assumed to be unopenable.

ques: what is your selection process for songs?
answ: first, generate some entirely new ones. then when i'm done doing that, then, go through the entire list of everything and find ones that i would be excited about doing, and put those in a 'finalists' list. like the play-offs, in sports. top 20 or 30. Then, i actually start working on the writing for some of those, without choosing yet. Then i set a hard deadline, sometime in the next 24 hours, to decide which will be the next one to be finished, recorded, vidified etc. It gets pretty painful toward the end, and sometimes there is a lot of feelings of remorse and dread the next day. but in the end i have to trust the system because it's the best system i have

ques: I'm a high school music teacher, and I get the sense that you avoid talking about your school years because you've realized what pretty much every musician needs to realize at one point or another if they are going to improve their musicianship. That the only person who can improve your musicianship is you. You have to the do the work, the ear training, the practicing, the time song writing and creating. So here's my question(s). How did you develop your work ethic for creating music?
Did people in your life have an influence on you developing this skill?
What do you think music teachers could be doing better to try and foster this skill in other people?
answ: it's similar to the way a person might develop a habit of using crack-cocaine, except instead of 1 drug it's more like 1000, because there is at least 1000 different ways to become totally and deeply hooked into music

i was able to hear a lot of music on records (and through the television of course, paired with visuals in such a way that i may not even realize until decades later just how crucial the audio-visual relationship is) and i will confess i also had access to a piano/keyboard instrument, and a drum set. There were also guitars around, but i've always been a bit overwhelmed/intimitated by guitars. having an extremely early start, it was pretty natural to find myself in many many personal and professional music relationships with peers (well at first it was usually people much older than me because i was so young to start)

what i think is the best approach, for me personally, is to write and record the best songs i can. if i can get them good enough, then maybe that will help someone else hear just a glimpse of what may be possible, just the way i might have heard someone else before, even if it's just for 7 seconds coming out of a car window going around the corner

ques: I struggle between choosing to spend my time coming up with new ideas or finish existing ones that I started. I want to have a goal of 1 new musical idea per *reasonable amount of time*, but I don't know how to prioritize between investing time into new things when I have ideas outstanding that need attention. Do you have any suggestions/have you experienced this? thanks
answ: basically what i did, when i was first in your situation, is to just keep coming up with new ideas. let them pile up. This is probably because i may have had a fear of not having enough ideas. Then it rapidly became a problem. Another thing i began doing is writing songs entirely on paper, and i would demand to finish the whole thing in 1 session. That's one way of dealing with it. so i wrote more and more and more. Sometimes they wouldn't get finished, sometimes they would. Usually if it was shorter, it would get finished. but they all got put into the list regardless. more years went by with more writing like this. It was more rare that i would ever record any of them. Eventually when the problem became even more serious, i finally found a way to work on the existing ideas. This is a whole separate task from generating new ideas, and i still consider them separate. For a couple years i ONLY did 'middle writing', which is where i work on existing ideas. Then a few months later, as i was getting ready to start recording some of them, i did a few weeks of finishing, just finishing writing for songs. I could talk for years about the different systems i've used for SELECTING which ones to work on. And this is not even to discuss selections for the recording process, which you didn't ask about. Eventually as enough years go by, you start to feel your life running out, so you probably take drastic measures. Nowadays, for me this is how it works: new ideas can come any time, that's always true. Sometimes they even come in dreams. So i catch them whenever they arrive, and i don't really do a writing session at that time because it's usually not the right time. but you just try to catch as much as you can. That's totally separate from any writing process or work process. Separately from that, it is a linear process of working toward the item i am releasing next, and i work on that 1 item until it's done. For songs, first what i do, at the beginning of a project, i do a round of new song idea generation, but this is NOT necessarily promising that any of these will be the one that's used. This is just to ensure that i am giving myself a chance to generate new ideas, which might have a chance of getting picked. So i generate some new ideas, maybe 10 or 15. Sometimes i use various different methods, just to make sure i've given myself a chance to try various things. Then, when that's done, i do song 'selection', which is where i'm going to choose which one is going to be recorded, for the next release. This selection is made from the ENTIRE list, which includes the new ones but also includes all the other ones, which are all at various levels of completion (writing). Once a selection is made, then it's quite simple. I finish the writing all the way, first, then record it, all the way. then make the video, all the way. I should clarify that this procedure didn't become solidified until after many many many years of ambiguity which may be similar to what you are going through now

ques: there seems to be a recurring pattern with your song lyrics in that many songs are about themselves. does "moon cheese" fit into this as well?
maybe tasting represents achieving the song's full potential, if you were doubting yourself at the time.
answ: it probably does

the whole point of that song, from the start, is the title. i was envious of other songs (probably country songs) which have a title which already has some cleverness baked right in. so i thought of one, "the moon is made of cheese (but i can't taste it)". so just went from there and tried to continue the game. you can't taste it, but you like the way the texture feels when you lick the surface. Makes perfect sense, but is also completely ridiculous. so the next line "the rumors start to go round the world that i'm crazy" well of course, because you're licking the moon. but no, instead, it's "becaususe you can't taste the cheese". so the fun score, for me, continues to be upheld up to that point. Next stanza, start with a line to echo the same theme as the first. famous phrase ('the grass is always green') then change it ('but i just changed it'). From this point, the key changes start to play an even more significant role, but, the game remains the same. i'm simply in search of quality songwriting

ques: Do you have any advice to someone who wants to write complete songs (with backing and harmonies and bridges) solo?
How do you start your writing process?
I have lots of ideas that I've recorded but I'm not really sure how to put them together.
answ: keep a journal. this could be a long journey
i pick an idea from the list

if they weren't written together, then they probably are not part of the same song. i think if you try to put them together they may look like awkward surgery. So, pick 1, and then 'play doctor' with it. give it a diagnosis. Is it the beginning of the song? is it not the beginning of the song? is it a 'chorus'? is it not a chorus? What does this idea mean to you? try to remember everything about the circumstances of coming up with it. This should lead you to your next decision about what it needs. Another thing that i should mention about the way i do it, i always write the entire song all the way through before even touching the production process. I know that not everyone does it this way, but, i've found out, to play to my strengths it's important to remain as nimble as possible during the writing process, and that means not trying to actually produce it while writing. i am a 'write first' person, then produce what i wrote. Also another thing i should mention, i was in your situation (wanting to produce entire songs myself) and i knew i was qualified, because i had already been playing multiple instruments for at least 10 or 15 years before, so i thought it should be easy. but unfortunately it took me at least 10 MORE years after that before i really felt like i could comfortably get the entire job done. actually i'm still not really there yet. But who knows ..... maybe you will find a way to make things.... simpler

answ: Remove all parts from the carton and separate them into part number groups as indicated in the parts list. To begin assembly, place the 5-star base upside down and insert casters into the bottom of base. Turn the base right side up on the floor and insert the cylinder into the center hole on the base. Place the telescoping cover over the the cylinder and rest it on the base. Attach the seat plate to the bottom of the seat cushion (with front of seat plate facing the front of the seat cushion) by using 15/8" screws into the front holes of the seat plate and 7/8" screws into the rear holes of the seat plate and tighten the screws. Align the back cushion with the seat cushion by positioning the back support plate over the seat plate with 11/4" screws. Do not tighten the screws completely. Attach the arms respectively on each side onto the bottom of the seat cushion and the sides of back cushion by using 11/2" screws. Tighten all the screws. Remember to tighten the screws on the back support plate. Place the plastic caps into the two arm holes on each arm. Place the assembled chair on top of the cylinder and press down until fully engaged. Periodically (every 90 days) make sure that the screws are still fully tightened.

ques: Hi Bill, I've been writing a song, and I got to a point where I think there should be a chorus next, but I have no idea how I should continue the song into one. How do I write a chorus from what I've already written?
answ: coming up with these things is like lightning striking. You can't really guarantee that it happens, but, i can tell you everything i know so far about this. 1. it's most likely to happen when you run through the song, from the beginning, at the right tempo, without stopping 2. it gets more and more likely for it to happen the longer time it's been since you've heard the song. 3. this is unfortunate, because it's very time consuming to keep waiting until you haven't heard the song in a while, every time you hear it 4. try walking to the door of the room you are in, touching the door handle, and then returning to the instrument (or demo-recording you are working with) and do a run through. this may be an artificial way to help 'reset' if you don't have time to wait 5. if you're just not getting it, try to make categories of things, and try to rule them out. 6. for example, try continuing it to be the same as what came before. Hopefully you will get a strong signal "yes" or "no" from trying this. then you can rule that out, or in 7. try going to the most normal chord you haven't used yet. for example, if your verse is full of C and F chords, try G and see what happens 8. try something with dense melody/lyric (wordy). hopefully that will give you a strong 'yes' or 'no' signal 9. try something with very few words. see if you can rule that out or in 10. keep trying to categorically prove or dis-prove that a certain strategy is right or wrong 11. i forgot the most important thing which i should have said first, imagine a scene where your song takes place. then name something that could happen next. i should have mentioned this one first because it's probably the one that's most likely to work

ques: Hey, Bill. So, I've reached that point in life in which I should know where I'm heading for, but I don't. I'm seventeen and apparently yesterday I couldn't choose what I'd have for lunch, but today I'm supposed to decide what to do for the rest of my life?

And I've had this idea in the back of my mind for years, but I feel like I used to be scared of not knowing what to do and now I'm just kinda scared of knowing I don't want to do anything. Growing up, I've developed real interst in mathematics and languages, and I always thought I'd do something related to one of these areas. But now that I actually have to choose, I don't want either.

I live in a developing country and everything is focused in applicability: maths and languages courses are too much about applied knowledge, never seen as pure areas of study. The reason why I fell in love with maths and languages in the first place was by overanalyzing things that have no real impact in the world: I liked that they were beautiful on their own, with no need to ever be used. And the prospects for me are really negative from this point on, because I feel like every college I go to and every job available for me will be quite the opposite of that. I wish I lived in the US or Europe where pure sciences actually exist, but I don't, and I can't afford to go these places. I feel like there's nothing I want to do with the rest of my life, and yet my parents say I have to choose soon because I gotta make money somehow.

Anyway, I know this completely out of the scope of this page, I just really needed someone to talk to. I guess my question is "what should I do given that I'm a broken piece in the machine of human existence and don't seem to have any use to anyone or be able to perform any useful service to humanity, however small?"
answ: there's no reason you should have to do that today. You may have known some of it since you were 6, and you may not find some of it until you are 96
you don't have to choose. those are both cool things, and they are allowed to be in your life, as much or little as you want

i think you will still get a chance to do many things with your life, besides the things you do for employment. Sure, make some decisions on that now, but just make the best decision you can, based on the information you have. even if if you don't have all the information. Because you are obviously still missing at least half of the information. most people are. but you will find a lot of that information along the way. And either one you choose, you'll probably learn something. and also keep in mind that some of the most powerful things to be learned, may come from outside the 'curriculum'

ques: um okay so hi person I look up to quite a bit idk if you'll see this but I kinda need some life advice and I don't know who else I can talk to but uhhh: I've always known that I am the kind of person who HAS to be producing some kind of creative output, whether it's something like art or dancing or getting a job... like I just kind of have to DO something with my life you know?? the problem is that I'm not skilled in any sort of particular area and I know that I need to pick something to do and then stick to it
but I just don't know what??? I consume and consume all the sights and events and media around me and I have all of these thoughts and desire to do SOMETHING

but I can't figure out what to channel it into. Once I figure out what I should be doing I know I'll put my blood, sweat, and tears into it but I just can't find a starting point. I'm also at the age where I need to start planning what to do with my life

and how to make money and shit but I just disappoint everyone who wants things from me because I can't stay motivated because I just don't have a PURPOSE. I just wish I had something I could be proud of and that I could be respected or respect myself for, something I poured all this energy I have inside me into, something that I can die with satisfaction knowing that I did.
I don't even know what kind of advice you could give me lol, but honestly if you have any thoughts or anything at all it would be really cool :)
answ: wait, that's not true. One of the coolest things about our universe is the way things can change

yes, this is good. you are getting charged up. You will probably experience some high passions and maybe a lot of envy and jealous rage, at this time. jealous of the people whose content you are consuming, because you really would like to be the one creating the content. At least that has been my experience
that's every age

with the amount of passion you have already demonstrated, you are going to find this in copious quantities, throughout your life. When in this moment it may seem like these 'purposes' are in 0 places, pretty soon you will find them in infinite places. infinity has a weird tendency to look like 0 sometimes. i think the first step is to be aware of this fact (at least it was for me). which is to realize that massive possibilities and potential exists literally everywhere, in everything. For me, i've dedicated my life to proving this, but before i felt like i had done it, i was always searching for any time i felt like someone else had proved it, and latch onto that and study it and use it as proof that it can be done.

I feel i should probably stop telling everyone to "write" a lot, because maybe some people just don't enjoy witing. But .... for you, it seems like you are perfectly comfartable writing, as you've just demonstrated. So i think you should find your most comfortable writing tool (a text editor on a computer, wherever you are most comfortable writing/typing), and just start.... USING it. Do anything you can in it. Use it to be honest. Use it to paint pictures. i don't care what you use it for, .... anywhere between honesty and art, fiction to diagrams, .... i mean, just test the keyboard, to start out with. Make sure every key is working. This will be one of the simplest ways to get your brain to start putting things into the world. Basically what we need to do is open up these pathways so your brain can start communicating with the world and putting things out there. you've demonstrated clearly that you are in the sort of 'consuming' stage, with some pent up desire to be the one on the other end of that. Maybe watch some film directors interviews on youtube. That could be a starting place. You might not want to direct films, but it might remind you of something else you do want to do. But another thing i should remind you, finding these things is like a river. You just make your best guess and do a thing, and then along the way you will hear some signals that will give you another hint of what you should try next. Trust me, these rivers ALWAYS get to huge dank oceans, eventually, if you let them flow. And you have made it clear that you have a huge amount of water to start with

ques: how did you highlight the globe for hotewig? on a 2d map, you mask the section and change the hue. in order to project the map onto the globe, do you need to do a UV mapping?
answ: the best way i found, was to export 2 versions of the same 3D clip. First you have to make an alternate map. Take the world map you're using (probably an equirectangular, 1 by 2 rectangle), and make a second map, with everything blacked out except your desired region. Then, swap in that map to the globe, then re-render the exact same clip, with the exact same camera movement, in the exact same time range. Then, when you import those clips to your 2D program, put the region/black map on top. then key out the black. then fuck the colors as desired

ques: hi bill. when making music, making ideas and stuff comes easy but when I try to revise them I just never get it done. my teacher and my parents push me to revise my works, but it's hard to find motivation. any thoughts? (btw you're amazing)
answ: the risk in 'revising' is that it might make it worse and less genuine. The benefit, however, is that it might make it more coherent. I spent a long time being unable or afraid to do this. i just kept writing new things. but eventually i just got so jealous of 'normal' songs, for having a repeating chorus, etc, that i figured it out. Half of the struggle, i think, is just choosing which item you're going to work on. for me it was necessary to first gather all the items into a list. Then i would go through the list one at a time, and make a few moves on each one. the 'diagnosis' is important. Play through the existing material, get a first impression, see if you generally like it or if it sucks, .... then start diagnosing it. If it's a small idea, figure out if it's the beginning or not the beginning. If it's already a long / complete idea, just go through from the beginning and find the first place where it truly sucks or is not good enough. This point is what i call the 'split point', the point where the existing material stops being good enough. So you put the rest aside, and write from there. I generally don't think it's good to plan on writing to connect to what comes after -- very risky and strange to do this. But it might happen automatically. so you can be open to that, but, plan on just writing from the split point and doing what's truly right from the split point

ques: At the beginning of your most recent song, "got some money", when you say "and I wonder if I'm sad about the money that I have, what is the music there. Is there any name for it. Where it gets lower and lower and with the little bit at the end.

answ: the best names i have for it is just the names of all the notes and chords. the notes are E, D#, C#, C in the melody. then i think you probably want to put the bass with it on the same notes, for beef, except on "have", i am definitely using a chord known as G#dominant7, and the important part of that chord in this case will be: you want the C note (melody) then you also want the F# note with that, somewhere in the harmony, and then you'd have G# in the bass. And i can't remember if i put the bass in G# (root of the chord) or C (with the melody), let me listen and check. ok yes the bass is on G#. Also i've harmonized the melody a 3rd above, so "money that i" will also have notes G#, F#, E, and then it seems for "have", instead of harmonizing a 3rd above, for that one i've used F# as the harmony note, as i said, to get the best results on that chord you need the F# and C notes to give it that twang. with the G# in the bass.

again, i can just tell you the notes. there's hardly any chords in here, except "mad". the bass is just wandering toward the important note (the "mad" chord), and the chord for mad could be pretty much described as D7 (D dominant7), and in this case, to get the sound you want there, really all you want is the note F# (in the melody), you want C also in the harmony, and you want D in the bass. that should do the trick

ques: Any tips for learning bass?
answ: throw yourself into a professional working band as soon as possible. But, in case it is a disease year, here's something else i can recommend: take your favorite songs, and delete the bass. This is pretty easy to do if you have a phone, tablet, or laptop. just play it without any headphones, and it automatically deletes the bass. then, make sure your bass IS plugged into something that is large so you can actually hear it (like an amp) and play along. Generally what i'm trying to say, get yourself into a situation where you are actually playing the bass role in songs, as soon as possible. that's pretty much where you are going to learn everything. Start out by just playing the root note of each chord (for example, if the chord is C, play the C note). Try to hold back from doing anything else just yet. but then pretty soon, as if by magic, you're automatically going to start doing everything you need to do and have a wild time

ques: how do you prime factor 1021
answ: see if the digits add up to 3, which they don't, then check for 7, so ditch the 21 and see if the 10 is a multiple of 7 which it's not, then check for 11 by subtracting it from 1021 which makes 101 (after you drop the zero at the end) and check if 101 is a multiple of 11 which you should know it's not because 101 is prime, then check for 13 by adding 39 to 1021 which makes 106 (after you drop the zero at the end) then divide by 2 to get 53 and check if that's a multiple of 13 which of course it's not because it's neighbor 52 already is, then check 17 by eliminating the 102 from the left of 1021 and you're left with 1 which is not a multiple of 17, then check 19 by adding it to 1021 and you get 104 (after dropping the zero at the end) and you probably already know 104 is not a multiple of 19 (divide it by 2 a few times and you'll just get to 13), then check 23 by adding 69 to 1021 to get 109 (after you drop the zero) which is prime so 23 is out, then check 29 by adding it to 1021 which makes 105 (after you drop the zero) which you might already know as just 7x15 so no 29s there, then you can check 31 by subtracting it from 1021 which makes 99 (after you drop the zero) and we all know that 99 is just 11x9 (without any 31s in it), then you can check 37 except i THINK we're already done because i think 37 squared is already higher than 1021 because 32 squared is 1024 (famously) so 37 squared can't be any lower than that. and if 37 squared is higher than 1021, then that means we're never gonna find any other prime factors higher than that, because, if we did, their partner factor would have to be something lower and we checked everything lower already, so 1021 is prime, so your answer is an earth shattering 1x1021

ques: when you said you could see that 262147 didn't have a 7 in its factorization, how did you know that? since there is no easy rule for divisibility by 7
answ: you can legally knock off the 7 from the right side. and it still will or won't be divisible by 7. do you see what i mean? so, imagine if you could make legal moves like this, until eventually you got it down to something you could recognize. So you can knock the 7 off. then you still have a 14 on the end. so obviously you can subtract 14 and you'll still be left with the same status of 7-ness (or non.) Then you're left with 262, and of course you can divide it all you want and that won't change the 7-ness either. so go ahead and divide it by 2, which is super easy, digitally. just halve the digits and it's 131. Ok so i already know that one is prime just because i know my primes up to at least there. but if you didn't know 131, you can of course subtract 21 (again, that won't change the 7-ness of the main number). so that brings you to 110 and you can drop the zero (again, dividing (by 10) won't change its 7-ness). so you drop the zero and it's 11, and please tell me you can tell by looking at it if 11 is divisible by 7 (it's not). so the original number couldn't have been, because we've only made legal moves up to here

So i knew it was going to be somewhat of an odd case, a frankenstein project, that would have to be pieced together cleverly to combine old and new. a bit too complicated of an endeavor for me to attempt in the first go. in addition it obviously required character animation, for continuity purposes, which actually i was quite ready for because i developed most of that in early 2020. but i still wasn't ready for it yet. i tried a cameo in the 'sun' song to prepare

ques: So how come you made the chorus for "la de da de da de da de day oh" in 2010,
but the rest of the song way later? Did you just read through your old notes and went "this is pretty darn good, I can use this"? And did you do the same for here comes the sun?
answ: i did not, that part was made in 2012. the verse before it was made in 2010

it's like a much much more meticulous and complicated version of that. i can write much faster than i can produce, so from 2008 to 2012 there was sort of a writing epidemic going on, where i just kept writing and writing and writing. not necessarily even finishing them. so in september 2012 i started gathering a chronological list of every song or partial song i had ever written, and then i started working little bits on each one. the same list continues to this day. So when it's time to record/produce and song/video, i have an elaborate writing/selection process where i write some brand new things first, add them to the list, then go through the entire list, pick out good candidates for the next production (i usually end up choosing about 25), then i do some additional writing on some of those, then finally i make my final selection. Then i continue writing that one to completion. The idea of casually finding a song, and just thinking 'oh this is good so i'll do it' seems hilarious to me. that's just not how it works. my mind has to go to full scale war with itself to settle on a song selection

ques: Hey bill. So I've read a lot of other questions about writing melodies/lyrics at the same time. I have applied it and got some nice verse melodies with lyrics I like too. answ: anything can happen, but the only way you're gonna get the answers is if you can trick your brain to stop worrying about it. which gets more and more difficult the more you care. which, if you're like me, is a lot. ques: do you think the louder you get a mix, the tighter the volume levels have to be for its elements? sometimes i want to just put a "maximizer" on my master and realize as soon as i start pumping everything, the unbalances become more noticeable, the loud start feeling louder in comparison to the mix etc. im not sure if its the maximizer, just the volume perception, or what.
answ: i am guessing it's not working properly. if it's doing what it's supposed to, it should even out the volume. it might be just making everything louder, because the settings might not be right for your mix and you might just be hearing the 'make up gain' by default, which would just make it louder and not do anything. (this is what happened to me in the early stages). what i would suggest is to make sure there is no make up gain, then make sure the ratio is not 1:1 (make sure the first number is higher), then raise the threshold all the way up. Now it should be doing exactly nothing. then press the bypass button on and off to compare, and it should sound exactly the same. Also check to see if there is a 'reduction' monitor so you can see when it's actually doing something. So now it should be doing nothing. Now, with the bypass off (so the compressor is ON), start gradually lowering the threshold until you start to see the 'reduction' meter gradually start to light up when it hits those loud parts, and it should be tapering them down. then once you've compressed it down a little then you can raise the make up gain

ques: how do you find/make all of the cool instruments in your music? i have a hard time finding good instruments to use.
answ: here's a good trick i use: shorten the release and the attack. most sounds you will find, to start off, are a total mess, with a really long attack and release. probably meant for someone who doesn't really play the keyboard that much and just wants to achieve success by holding down 1 note. But when i shorten up the attack and release, then that very quickly turns it into something that is delightful for me to play, as a keyboard player. Another thing you can do is program in something on one of the wheel controls. my 2 favorite options for this are filter cutoff (wawawawaw), and vibrato. To do a nice vibrato the way i like, set the LFO to somewhere around 4x per second, then make the LFO control the pitch up and down, then, set the wheel to increase the depth of the LFO as you push the wheel up. If you have things on the wheels then i think you're gonna have a lot of fun and be able to express yourself really well

ques: How do you learn to figure out what different chords are by ear?
answ: go through about 50 of your favorite songs, and identify each chord with brute force. quickly unpause/pause (or nowadays you can edit to loop a tiny fraction of audio very quickly) and just pick it out note by note and put it together. write down all the chords to a song (in time, with bar lines, etc.)..... once you do this for about 30 or 40 songs, i think you will find that you don't have to search for the individual notes anymore. ... maybe not even pause it at all. After about 100 more songs, you probably won't even have to listen to the song, you will be able to do it from memory. after about 1000 songs, you will probably be able to hear someone singing the melody for a song you have never heard before, without hearing the chords, and figure out what the chords should be. after 10,000 songs, you should be able to play chords along with them on the first try, never having heard the song before, and have them think you already knew the song

ques: can you explain what the chords are for the song I like? I think it's really catchy and I would like to learn the song, but I can't figure out the chords. Thanks!
answ: i have good news and bad news. The good news is, i have the original chart of when i wrote it, all on paper, years before i ever recorded it. The bad news is, it's not guaranteed to be entirely accurate because when i record a song, i am potentially allowed to invoke the 'suck' clause and change some of the details IF i thought it sucked. but the good news is, i'm looking at the chart right now and it seems extremely accurate. the bad news is that the end was re-written (not shown on this chart) but the good news is that the new ending is only 4 bars, in replacement of 27 bars on the chart, and those new 4 bars, if they were written in this chart language, would not have shown any chords, it would be notated as rap only, in a similar notation language to the 27 bar ending you do see. so you wouldn't have seen any chords from the chart there anyway. The bad news of course, is that for sections like that, in this chart language, you never see any chords, and chordal decisions for those types of sections are made during the recording. However the good news is that the only other part like this would be the intro, and i think i actually did not use any chords there in the recording either. However the bad news is, for that new 4 bar section which occurs in the recording but not the chart, there IS chordal information there (arranged when recording) that would certainly NOT be reflected in the chart. Also the other bad news is that the final recording is not guaranteed to be done in the same key as the chart, BUT the good news is, in this case it actually was. The good news is, i'm pretty sure i must have some sort of document somewhere that indicates the writing of those last 4 bars, either a written update or a recorded writing demo, but the bad news is i can't seem to find it and now i think it doesn't exist, and it seems more likely that i was feeling brave enough to actually re-write a 4 bar ending on the spot, in the recording session, which is a rare occurence but not impossible. The good news is i just found the written update which contains the last line written at the end. and i can say for certain that you are supposed to cross out the entire line before "v2" and also cross out everything up until that new line. the only reason i probably didn't cross it out is because i knew i was already recording it so i didn't need to make note of that change. but i can assure you that i never intended for that additional 4 bars to be in addition to the other 27. they are intended to replace everything from "get it" and after. so with some assembly required, you can take the original page 1 from here, then cross out the last 27 bars and REPLACE it with the last 4 bars of this page. and the extra 27 bars remains as a bonus alternate ending, which should NOT include the final 4

ques: I've noticed you have lots of sheets and charts for some of the stuff you write. how important do you finding writing music down on paper to be? I have a traditional music background and a bachelors degree in music but when I'm actually doing stuff I ~like~ to do like song writing and recording little tunes I hardly ever write anything down minus the words and chords
answ: if you're brave enough to believe you can remember the exact melody, then that's fine. i don't like to take any chances with that. i've watched people come up with a brand new awesome idea, and then play the same thing for me again tomorrow and the melody has changed and they don't realize it, and the original was definitely better. Because new song ideas are so new, you haven't heard them very much, so you are likely to forget exactly how it went. i am not comfortable trusting that the next time i look at it i'll remember the exact melody. so i must document it exactly. Whether this is done with notation or not, it doesn't really matter to me. it can be done with recording references, and nowadays i always use recording references, because we live in such a digital world. but for a long time i was using handwritten notation. The only times i ever do it with notation is when i have no instrument near me. i used to go to the library and put in earplugs and write songs that way. nowadays, when writing songs at the keyboard, i just make recorded references and cite them in the lyric sheet. The same goal is accomplished: to exactly document the lyric, melody, and chords
