ques: hi, what happens when i makin a song but i make the melody but i forget to put words to it, but now i am at the melody and i don't know how to figure out what words to attach? did i fuck it up?
answ: first, you must try to convince the song you are actually NOT trying to write it. make up a contract agreement that you and the song can sign, that says "i am NOT trying to 'write' this song, and will not make any attempts to do so!" and you and the song both sign it, and maybe you'll have some fine print located somewhere near the bottom of your left shoe or something. Then, as you sit down casually next to your melody, 'NOT' appearing to have any intention or desire to write the song, .... just begin trying phrases and sentences with the melody. don't worry about what's "good" or not yet, just start saying anything that comes to mind, with that melody. You will automatically start getting a feel for what the mechanics are (lyrically) of this melody. you'll see which kinds of words and phrases seem to always want to go in certain parts. and you'll just be internalizing the melody subconsciously, in the linguistic part of your mind. Then, put that aside, and just tell a story in your own words of what this melody is. When did you think of it? how did it make you feel? describe anything you know or feel about this melody and its origins. Sometimes you can even catch a glimpse of the exact essence of what the melody seems to be saying, even if it's the totally wrong number of words or syllables and has no physical resemblence to the shape or size of the melody. if you get this, definitely write it down. just try to PARAPHRASE (non-musically, in normal non-lyrical language) exactly what you think the melody seems to feel like it's saying. Now at this point the song will probably start to think you are trying to write it, with all the effort you've been putting in, so you will probably need an updated contract to assure everyone even more clearly that you are 'NOT' 'TRYING' to 'write' the song. then after that it's pretty much a waiting game. if you can stay calm and be patient enough for the song to forget you are trying to write it, that's when it's gonna happen

ques: What kind and/or how much vocal training have you had?
answ: never understood most vocal training, because i found breathing to be so connected to thought, i've always found it difficult to really control your breathing/air directly. so vocal triaining mostly never made sense to me in that way. so i was stuck on my own, and yet i sounded terrible. so that left me to figure out what to do. i quickly realized that there is a phenomenon at play here which is very similar to acting. you have to convince your inner-most mind to actually believe in the things you are communicating. A neat hack i found was to improvise the lyrics. i always seemed to sound much better when the words were genuinely made up at the time i'm singing them, instead of scripted. and if they are scripted, you have to ask a lot of similar questions that an actor would ask, about your character and your situation that you are trying to envoke. but aside from that, i also found out later that simply the more time singing makes you better. then much later on, a voice doctor told me that clearing your throat is bad, so i stopped doing that, and i also picked up a boring warm up exercise which i do on morning walks

ques: im best friends with my own front door activates this part of my brain i can never reach. it's amazing. it's the bent key that somehow unlocks the safe to gold and crack. specifically talking about 1:40 to the end, all the lines connect together so perfectlyHOW WAS THIS MASTERPIECE MADE. i want the full backstory. maybe some lines from the timestamp i said would do..
answ: this is exactly what happened. all my life i've struggled with the reality that it takes me much much much longer than i wish it takes, to produce anything. years go by and i'm fighting to reach a reasonable pace, and never seem to succeed. well, one day i suddenly snapped, took a desperate walk outside, got angry and screamed at the sky a little (in my mind), and just said '2 weeks or die trying'. the thing is, i'm sure i've tried saying this before, but sometimes the stars align and it works. so the first part of doing any song is song selection. i go through my list of songs, which have a writing % completion of anywhere from .1% to 100%. and i have to choose one. this is normally almost impossible for me, and to do it right, i have to spend many days on it. i went through maybe 50% of the list, and it felt like none of them were really working for me at the time, and i felt a bit pressured to do it quickly (because of the 2 week challenge i was doing), and so in a snap decision, i said 'what song do i WISH i was doing', and i was able to trick myself into imagining the first line. so that was cool, felt like i was off to a roaring start, and then suddenly a day went by and i hadn't made it out of the 'box' of that melody/chord sequence. in other words, i had maybe the first 6 lines, which, as you can hear, are all within the same exact musical figure. but what scared me most was that i had spent way too long and only come up with a few seconds. and i knew this was no way to beat the 2 week challenge. so essentially i realized that i had to finish the writing in 4 hours. so basically a ruthless burst of paranoid speed had to kick in. you can probably hear the brute force, desperation, and then attempts to deal with it, in the 'bad sign' part, and 'not gonna happen' part. basically i've hurled myself off the edge, into whatever comes next, before having earthly idea what would actually come next. so in that sense i was almost improvising (in the writing). To be clear, i'm talking about the writing, which is done entirely before the recording. so i'm not saying i improvised the song during recording. i always write the song first. but during the writing process it felt a bit like improvising because i had to write it so fast. So the next few sections sort of have their ups and downs, for better or for worse, because at this point i've convinced myself that there's no turning back, i have to just run, because there's no time. And inevitably, if you are able to truly adopt this attitude, it eventually finds its feet. and that seems to happen when it lands on the outvamp, and these last 16 bars seem to be an outpouring of the exact emotions i was dealing with, in the circumstances of the 2 week challenge and all the desperation leading up to it, and how i was dealing with it

ques: is there a reason that "memory" appears between aaaacv and frenca, then again between frenez and loveqa and yeat again between lovesz and zzzzya in the part of got some money where the 6-letter combinations are scrolling down the screen?
answ: yes. What i would have preferred to do, is to be able to actually create that entire alphabetical phrase list. which i was able to generate quite easily, but the problem we run into, when the list goes into the graphics, .... the list is so long that it actually makes the computer lag, or probably even crash, depending on how you do it. There's literally millions of lines in that text pattern, if it were carried out properly from a to z across all 6 characters. So even though it's just text, it actually is an absurdly unnecessary strain on the memory of the scene, pretty much any way you slice it. And the truth is, in that scene, with the small amount of time it's shown, you'd never see all the lines. and also, another reason you don't wanna include the whole list is that the scroll direction would become incoherently out of phase. like those car wheels on tv that seem to move slow or backwards or whatever. So it turns out, even just to create the proper looking downward scroll, you need to reduce the number of elements drastically. like pretty much skip 99% of the parts during the fast scroll. But this still does create a continuity problem, because if anyone sees the (maybe 1) frame where you can see it jump from A to L or whatever, .... i feel there's gonna need to be an explanation there. So my explanation is 'memory' as a place holder for the perhaps millions of lines we've skipped

ques: I know you like to try and catch all your ideas. I used to too. At work in the amazon warehouse many ideas came to me. and I would run around like a crazy person trying to find a pen and paper to write them down. then at home after a while I ended up having a stack of these ideas. then two stacks and three. then I went for yoga teacher training and learned about aparigraha and wanted to become detached and the feeling I get when an idea comes feels very attached so I wanted to get rid of my stacks of ideas. so I got rid of most of them and kept a few. But now I'm thinking, why do I need to capture every idea? because I'm not the source of them. The source is endless! and if the source wanted me to have an idea at a certain point in time, it would send one, right? so maybe that's how I can remain detached while also being open to receiving ideas. ques: Please give us the rest of the factorizing steps!
answ: i can't give them all at once, because there's way too many. but let's pick a random number up to a million and i'll try to tell you the first 3 things i would do. The number we're working with today is 306124. The first thing is, notice it's even. How do we know this? because the last digit is even. so first we gotta cut the whole thing in half. this can be done by slicing it where you see even numbers that you can handle. so for me that's 30 6 12 4. cut those in half, and keep them in the same order, preserving the digits. so that makes 15 3 06 2.... or 153062. Next, notice it's still even. do the same thing again. this gets tricky because you have a lot of consecutive odd numbers in there. cutting numbers in half when they have a lot of odd digits, without paper, can be a little annoying. but if you can handle the 1530, then the 62 part is easy. 1500 in half is 750, plus the 15 is 765. and the 62. so 76531. Now it's odd and you can't divide it anymore. So you can go ahead and put some 2's in your final answer, because you divided it by 2, twice. so you know that your answer is going to include 2 twice. Now, you're left with an odd number: 76531. The next step is to check if it's divisible by 3. The trick for this is, and most people seem to know this trick, if the number is divisible by 3, all the digits are gonna add up to a multiple of 3. so you can group them. so, looking at 76531, .. knock out the 6, i can knock out 7 and 5 (75, mult of 3, or 57, either way, same thing) knock out the 3, ... and you're left with 1 which is non-3. so by knocking out digits and groups of digits which add to 3 or mult of 3, if all the digits got knocked out that way then we know it's a mult of 3, but if we were left with any non-3s, (which we were), then we know it's not a mult of 3. Ok, now the real game begins. We're going to check every other prime number, in ascending order. No need to check 5, because we can see that it's not a multiple of 5 (hopefully you can see that outright ... but the way to tell that is if the last digit is 0 or 5, which it's not). So next we're going to check 7. Every prime we're going to check from here on out will be based on the same system. We're going to manipulate the main number (76531) by adding or subtracting the checker as many times as we want. IF the main number is a mult of 7, then that means we can add or subtract 7 as many times as we want, and it should STILL be a mult of 7. We can ALSO DIVIDE the main number by ANYTHING and it should still be a mult of 7, if it originally was. So basically the idea is to do these manipulations in a way that gets you to something you recognize as a mult of 7 or not. There are many ways of doing this. First, if you want, you can just drop the 7 from the left. because this essentially would mean you're subtracting 70000. which, if the original number was a mult of 7, then it should still be a mult of 7 when you subtract 70000. so we'll knock out the 7, and you have 6531. Next, i'm going to do probably the most common technique, which is to work from the right. Here's an interesting principle: if we've already reduced the main number in the ways we've already reduced it (cut it in half until it's odd, divide by 3 until it's not a mult of 3, divide by 5 until it's not a mult of 5), then THAT MEANS that for ANY future prime number you wanna check, you can ALWAYS cause the number to level off with a zero at the end by either adding or subtracting THE CHECKER OR ITS TRIPLE. That's because all your future prime numbers that you're gonna check are gonna end in either 1,3,7, or 9. So that means those are always either 1 or 3 away from 10. And if you've already reduced your main number properly, then that number will ALSO always be either 1 or 3 away from the nearest 10. So you just pick which maneuver to make based on what you need. So looking at our main number as it stands now, 6531, and if we're checking for 7, i can tell you that what you wanna do is subtract 21. That's how you can get it to level off to a zero at the end. 6510. and of course you can drop the zero, because that does NOT change whether or not the main number is divisible by 7. so that leaves you with 651. the same move again works: subtract 21, gets you to 630 and drop the zero, you have 63. Do you recognize it yet, as something that you know to be a multiple of 7, or something you know to not be a multiple of 7? you might recognize 63 as a multiple of 7. But in case you don't see that, you could make another move, by adding 7, and you get 70, drop the zero, is 7. Now do you recognize it (7) as either being a multiple of 7 or non-multiple of 7? i think you do. So we can confirm that 7 is one of the factors. next comes the not so fun part where you have to actually divide 76531 by 7. then when you get the result, continue working with this new main number, and you also have to check 7 again on that number in case it's in there twice
